subject.title: [Feature]: Self-evolving SOUL.md via opt-in reflection sub-turn + soul_update tool

question: Should OpenClaw core accept opt-in model-mediated writes into SOUL.md, and what security/product boundary must that feature meet before the linked PR can merge?
rationale: The request crosses durable instruction context, session state, config, CLI, tool exposure, and channel-notice semantics; automation cannot choose the permanent SOUL persistence contract for maintainers.

options.title: Accept core feature after hardening
options.body: Proceed with the linked PR only after the tool is privately gated, policy-ordered, visibly noticed, reversible, and covered by hostile-input and upgrade tests.

options.title: Move preference capture to memory/plugin path
options.body: Keep SOUL.md manual and use memory plugins or a plugin API extension for automatic durable preference capture instead of core instruction-file mutation.

options.title: Decline automatic SOUL mutation
options.body: Close the feature direction if maintainers decide that model-mediated SOUL.md writes are too risky or outside core scope for now.

recommendation.title: Accept core feature after hardening
recommendation.body: Proceed with the linked PR only after the tool is privately gated, policy-ordered, visibly noticed, reversible, and covered by hostile-input and upgrade tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about product/security architecture, and this history includes the SOUL guide plus memory ownership boundary work.
